Latest Update: Front Office: Radhi Devlukia

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Radhi Devlukia isn’t afraid of tears.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, two years into the show, Devlukia, a best-selling author, cook, and founder of beverage manufacturer Juni, is unveiling a upcoming studio and office space located within her and Shetty’s Los Angeles house.
  • In a recent development, from the start, Cooney knew what the space would not include.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Radhi Devlukia isn’t afraid of tears. On her podcast, A Really Good Cry, the whole point is to get personal, and to do so with guests as varied as supermodel Miranda Kerr, dermatologists, hospice nurses, personal finance advisors—and Devlukia’s husband, fellow podcaster Jay Shetty.

Recent findings suggest that now, two years into the show, Devlukia, a best-selling author, cook, and founder of beverage manufacturer Juni, is unveiling a upcoming studio and office space located within her and Shetty’s Los Angeles house. Devlukia turned to designer Jess Cooney, who has a namesake Berkshires-based interiors firm, to craft a space designed to support these really good cries. Cooney had never tackled a podcast studio before but was ready for the challenge, which included building a room that could both serve as a set—technical components, artificial light, and all—as well as a welcoming home office.

In a recent development, from the start, Cooney knew what the space would not include. “We wanted to move away from the tropes usually seen in podcast studios, like styled bookshelves or cluttered backgrounds that detract from the people being interviewed, and also anything logo or merch heavy,” she says. “And toward something that felt warmer and more inviting.”.

According to recent reports, instead, she took cues from spaces like fashion designer Bella Freud’s London apartment, Jean Cocteau’s Villa Santo Sospir in the Côte d’Azur, and Paloma Elsesser’s home by Gregory Rockwell. The resulting office, says Cooney, “has this incredible womb-like, feminine atmosphere that cocoons and holds you.”.

Below, Devlukia takes our Front Office survey, giving a behind-the-scenes look at her latest home base.

What’s your favorite part of the space?

Radhi Devlukia: The hanging art piece in the middle of the window, Kissed by Katie Burdon.

When you need to lock in and power through work, what’s your setup?

Doors open, facing the window, instrumental music playing. I also move areas a lot during work hours to stay focused, so sometimes I’m at the desk, sometimes on the swivel chairs, sometimes on the floor by the window!

What’s the oldest thing in your office?

It has been revealed that I have articles printed about my grandma and grandad on my canvas memory wall. They taught at schools in Africa in the 1970s and there were articles written about how much they were doing for the community. I also have vintage ceramics—I love the mix of old and new.

According to recent reports, it really depends. If there are two of us, we’re on the swivel chairs. If there are a few of us, we’re around the marble table. We love keeping things casual at the office so sometimes people sit on the cozy rug or wherever feels comfortable.

What was the best meeting you’ve had there?

We have had so many creative meetings in this office. It’s such a calming and flowing environment. The whole rebrand of the podcast was ideated in this new office, which I’m obsessed with now.

What would you change about it if you could?

Maybe just having the ability to shoot with the blinds open.

What’s the funniest thing that happened there?

My team loves to prank me, so there’s been a lot of laughter in our office!

It has been revealed that annie Goldsmith is the senior editor and digital lead at ELLE Decor, where she covers design, culture, style, and trends. She previously held positions at The Information, covering technology and culture, and Town & Country, writing about news, entertainment, and fashion. Her work has also appeared in Vogue, Rolling Stone, and the SF Standard.

Turns Out Chuck Schumer’s Bid for Senate Majority Leader Isn’t as Done a Deal as We Thought

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (357 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In January 1971, the members of the Democratic majority, in what was to be the 92nd Congress, met to determine who would lead them.
  • (The reformist impulse, however, continued to flow through the party, culminating in the reforms that resulted in the nomination of George McGovern for president in 1972.).
  • At the moment, it seems that the parallels are all in the Senate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In January 1971, the members of the Democratic majority, in what was to be the 92nd Congress, met to determine who would lead them. At the time, there was a rising faction of Democrats demanding congressional reforms, including newly introduced leadership. Speaker John McCormack, the ancient Speaker, had finally retired, elevating majority leader Carl Albert into the Speaker’s chair with little or no opposition. However, a serious fight erupted within the caucus over who would replace Albert as the next majority leader. The establishment choice was Representative Hale Boggs of Louisiana, while the reformists lined up behind Representative Morris Udall of Arizona. Boggs managed to squeak out a win, which elevated a Boston congressman named Thomas P. O’Neill to be majority whip, beginning his rise through the leadership.

(The reformist impulse, however, continued to flow through the party, culminating in the reforms that resulted in the nomination of George McGovern for president in 1972.).

At the moment, it seems that the parallels are all in the Senate. (Representative Hakeem Jeffries’s rise to Speaker seems safe.) Once again, we have solid Democratic majorities in the coming Congress facing off against a villainous Republican president. Once again, there is a reform-minded faction in the incoming Senate majority challenging Senator Chuck Schumer that has begun to coalesce behind Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland. The 67-year-old Van Hollen is an unlikely insurgent against Schumer, whose age is the primary strike against him. From the AP:.

However, Van Hollen has an undeniable streak of independence. He took on the administration boldly in the case of Kilmar Abrego García, the deportee from Maryland whom the administration used in a cruel game of hide-and-seek.

Van Hollen stood against some serious fire while advocating for Abrego García from the governments of both the United States and El Salvador. This included Salvadoran officials planting margarita glasses on the table at which Van Hollen and García sat during a photo opportunity. And, fundamentally, it’s just time for Schumer to step aside. The newly elected senators need new leadership, and if Van Hollen is the leader they want, then he should lead them.

Princess Kate Is Bright in Pistachio Green and Cobalt Blue as She Arrives in Mumbai With Prince William

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that princess Catherine and Prince William are starting their tour of India off strong.
  • Kate brought a colorful wardrobe for the mini trip with her husband.
  • She paired the blazer with a breezy white top, slim white trousers from McQueen, and black-and-beige flats with pearl-embellished buckles from Camilla Elphick for a fun game of street cricket.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that princess Catherine and Prince William are starting their tour of India off strong. Today, the royal couple arrived in Mumbai for their three-day state visit—their first joint one in four years. And as photos show, the pair is ecstatic to be there.

Kate brought a colorful wardrobe for the mini trip with her husband. She made her first public appearance this morning in a fresh pistachio-green blazer from Veronica Beard, and then changed into a bright cobalt-blue dress from Roksanda.

She paired the blazer with a breezy white top, slim white trousers from McQueen, and black-and-beige flats with pearl-embellished buckles from Camilla Elphick for a fun game of street cricket. Dangly crystal earrings and a matching teardrop necklace completed the daytime look.

Then, to take a ride on Mumbai’s Metro and to attend the Earthshot Prize Impact Assembly, Kate changed into her vibrant Roksanda midi dress—the same one she wore to the Wimbledon men’s final in July 2025.

The design has a pretty V neckline. short, structured sleeves with a bow-like detail on one shoulder, a belted waist, and a flowy skirt.

The Princess of Wales styled the dress with chocolate-brown accents: suede Gianvito Rossi heels and the small Hudson bag from DeMellier.

Finally, she upped the glamour with blue and gold jewelry, including a pair of lapis lazuli-and-diamond drop earrings by Indian jewelry brand Amrapali—pieces which she wore to a charity gala in Mumbai during her 2016 tour of India.

William and Kate are in Mumbai to attend the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Summit, but during their visit will also take the time to carry out engagements relating to sustainability, innovation, and the relationship between India and the United Kingdom.

#43152. Latest Update: The One Record in Sports That Will Never Be Broken

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (408 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: The One Record in Sports That Will Never Be Broken

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy.
  • According to recent reports, in this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey.
  • The first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one told me there would be math.

According to recent reports, back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy. Then suddenly, quite recently, numbers became paramount in sports. Baseball led the way, as it does in so many areas where boredom is involved. Now, thanks to gambling’s explosion in popularity, statistics have become one of the primary ways to be a fan.

According to recent reports, in this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey. It is this, which boggles the mind: Wayne Gretzky ended his career in 1999 with a total of 2,857 points, which includes goals and assists. Factor out the goals, and he’s still at 1,963, which is 42 more points than the player with the next-highest total, Jaromir Jagr, who is retired.

The first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers. These were the dynastic Oilers, loaded with talent: Mark Messier. Jari Kurri. Glenn Anderson. Grant Fuhr between the pipes. All of them Hall of Famers. Amid all this clamorous talent, Gretzky was a phantom. He had this strange and wonderful ability to vanish in the middle of the action and then, suddenly, appear in exactly the right spot at exactly the right time to make exactly the right play.

Sources indicate that gretzky will likely be the leading point scorer in NHL history for the next several decades. In fact, you have to go all the way down to seventh place on the list to find an active player, Sidney Crosby, who is 202 short of Gretzky’s 1,963 assist-only number. Another active player, Alex Ovechkin, is in tenth place, but he’s got one skate out the door already. The next active players on the list are Evgeni Malkin and Patrick Kane, at 23rd and 24th.

In a recent development, like Gretzky himself, this statistic disappears among all the more important numbers until it suddenly pops out to amaze and astound. I like Sidney Crosby a great deal as a player, but I hope he never gets there.

Charles P Pierce is the author of four books, most recently Idiot America, and has been a working journalist since 1976.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you look to celebrities like Anne Hathaway and Kate Middleton for style inspiration, you should be carrying around a DeMellier handbag. The British handbag label is known for its A-list clientele, understated aesthetics, and luxury quality at an accessible price point. To kick off its massive Black Friday sale, DeMellier is offering ELLE readers early access—use the code ELLE20 at checkout for 20 percent off sitewide, starting now.

Shop DeMellier’s Early Black Friday Sale.

In a recent development, as a longtime DeMellier fan, I’m here to guide you through the best celebrity-worn handbags to shop during the brand’s Black Friday sale. Many styles are expected to sell out when the event opens to the public on November 20, so it’s worth doing your shopping during ELLE’s early access period to secure your top picks.

Sources indicate that if you’re fresh to the brand, start with the label’s bestselling New York bag. The timeless silhouette comes in four sizes and over a dozen different leather, suede, and calf hair finishes. The east-west New York shoulder bag that Anne Hathaway carried during the Mother Mary press tour would make for a memorable holiday gift—though you’ll be tempted to keep it for yourself after experiencing the quality materials and construction IRL.

Earlier this year, Lindsay Lohan wore the full-sized Newly introduced York bag while filming the upcoming Hulu series Count My Lies. (A different DeMellier number Lohan wore on set has already sold out, so I can’t guarantee her brown leather tote will stay in stock, either.) Emily Ratajkowski, Gemma Chan, Emily Blunt, Katie Holmes, Renée Zellweger, and Reese Witherspoon have also been seen carrying DeMellier’s New York silhouette, should you need any more convincing.

Famously, DeMellier is a favorite bag brand of the British royal family. Kate Middleton has made more than ten public appearances with the Nano Montreal in tow. The Small Hudson bag the Duchess of Wales carried during a recent visit to India would make the perfect plus-one for holiday party outfits. Queen Camilla, Meghan Markle, and Princess Beatrice have also worn DeMellier bags, though their picks have sold out.

Sources indicate that earlier this year, Meryl Streep wore the full-sized version of Middleton’s Hudson bag during the Devil Wears Prada 2 press tour. Large enough for a laptop, the carryall makes a chic alternative to a traditional work tote and has also received the stamp of approval from Emma Roberts, Kristen Bell, and Elsa Hosk.

Recent findings suggest that the brand’s minimalist Stockholm silhouette has become another celebrity favorite—and it’s won over ELLE fashion editors as a work bag, too. Naomi Watts wore the versatile Stockholm shoulder bag while promoting Season 2 of All’s Fair. And if you need more convincing on this particular collection’s versatility, it’s been spotted on the likes of Rosie Huntington-Whiteley, Lili Reinhart, and Simone Ashley.

After close to a decade in the spotlight, nearly every DeMellier bag has found a celebrity fan, so there are no wrong choices. Browse other A-listers’ picks below, then head to the brand’s site for its full sale offering. And remember: Public access begins on November 20, and items return to full price on November 30, so be sure to grab your favorite style for a good deal while you can.

#43126. A Menorca Farmhouse Finds Its Easy Elegance

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (821 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elledecor ↗ Open Full Page

A Menorca Farmhouse Finds Its Easy Elegance

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Above: In the living room, López-Quesada replicated the original ceiling beams and finished the walls in traditional Menorcan lime plaster.
  • For Spanish designer Isabel López-Quesada, summers tend to revolve around Biarritz, in southwestern France, where she has a home.
  • Sources indicate that typically, López-Quesada goes there to relax and spend time with friends, but around five years ago she received a call from a Bilbao family who asked her to refresh their vacation home outside Mahón, Menorca’s capital.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: In the living room, López-Quesada replicated the original ceiling beams and finished the walls in traditional Menorcan lime plaster. A sofa of her design is grouped with a 1960s Tito Agnoli rattan daybed, a Mexican palm leaf stool, and a custom cocktail table upholstered with a Moroccan rug.

For Spanish designer Isabel López-Quesada, summers tend to revolve around Biarritz, in southwestern France, where she has a home. Still, she always carves out time for Menorca, regarded as the most laid-back of Spain’s Balearic Islands. That vibe suits the ELLE Decor A-list designer, whose signature style is luxurious but unfussy, harmonizing old and new with breezy refinement.

Sources indicate that typically, López-Quesada goes there to relax and spend time with friends, but around five years ago she received a call from a Bilbao family who asked her to refresh their vacation home outside Mahón, Menorca’s capital. An old farm property, or finca, the five-bedroom residence required extensive updates. López-Quesada was steadfast in preserving such historical elements as a well and donkey stables, which she transformed into an indoor-outdoor bathroom with a patio and marble tub. “It was vital to respect the style of Menorca,” she claims. “We were very careful with the materials, so it all goes together and conveys the sentiment I want the house to have.”.

López-Quesada founded her namesake studio as a precocious 20-year-old Madrileña 40 years ago. Initially inspired by her mother’s yen for decorating and the work of celebrated Spanish designers such as Paco Muñoz and Fernando Benjumea, López-Quesada garnered wide attention in the early 2000s, when she converted an old Madrid wax factory into an atelier and a luxurious home for her family, filled with antiques and contemporary pieces. Soon she had interest from clients all over the world. Today López-Quesada’s 12-person team includes one of her three adult children, daughter Isabel Llanza. Five years ago the pair co-founded the lifestyle brand Isita Home, selling products they make themselves or discover on their travels.

It has been revealed that the Menorca project began by gutting the house’s interior and rebuilding it “in an old style,” López-Quesada notes. Central to it all was adding custom windows and doors to each room so the island’s golden light could flood the spaces. Vaulted and beamed ceilings were left intact or were recreated. Reconfiguring the floor plan, López-Quesada eschewed a proper dining room in favor of an eat-in open kitchen. “Most of the time you are eating outside,” she says.

With Menorca’s unrelenting summer sun, bougainvillea-draped pergolas were a must for leisurely alfresco lunches and dinners. Swaths of white lantana and lily of the Nile border the terraces, while “the pool reflects the sky like a mirror and provides a refreshing feel,” López-Quesada notes.

Her collaborator on the gardens was Spanish landscape architect Luis González-Camino. “My vision was to design a water-efficient Mediterranean garden, divided into distinct yet connected ‘garden rooms’ for different seasons and times of day,” he notes. González-Camino preserved the property as a natural Mediterranean woodland, with wild olive trees providing cover.

Indoors, López-Quesada installed French terra-cotta floor tiles chosen for their aged look. The three fireplaces were all handcrafted in traditional Menorcan style—a little imperfect, painted white—and decorated with vintage tiles the designer keeps in her Madrid warehouse.

Recent findings suggest that she offset the white ceilings and lime plaster walls with vibrant textiles and tilework in blues and greens inspired by Menorca’s native palette. An upstairs bedroom is anchored by an iron four-poster bed with a blue-and-white-striped canopy; its bath has a shower lined with lapis-colored zellige tiles. Doors, which across Menorca are customarily painted in bold shades, here are finished in verdant hues.

Custom cabinets are designed with whimsically patterned cutouts for airflow, since humidity is a major factor. “On the islands, if you close the cupboards completely, mushrooms will grow inside,” López-Quesada notes.

Step Inside This Renovated Menorca Retreat.

She arrayed the spaces with a lively mix of vintage and newly introduced furnishings, emphasizing organic materials: rattan chairs, bamboo shades, Moroccan rugs, lots of linen and cotton fabrics in spirited florals or stripes. “If I use a heavy piece, then the rest is lighter,” she says. The tableware maintains the blue and green theme, including pieces from Isita Home and hand-blown glassware from neighboring Mallorca.

Recent findings suggest that in the end, the owners asked López-Quesada to redo their home in Spain’s Basque region as well. It’s one of several projects she currently has across the country, including reimagining a hotel in Barcelona, and she’s also designing homes in Paris, Shanghai, and the Dominican Republic. Many of her projects are with repeat clients. “That’s how it works,” the designer says. “It’s like a chain.”.

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 concern of ELLE Decor.

Sarah Cristobal is a writer, editor, and creative consultant. She is right now editor-at-large for 10 Magazine USA, among other freelance projects.

In a recent development, as you might imagine, my coworkers and I, well, we see a crap ton of clothes on a daily basis. We’re fashion editors, after all. Our working hours are spent poring over the latest collections, visiting showrooms to experience the pieces for ourselves, and analyzing every trend. All that said, we can be a tough bunch to impress. I mean that earnestly. But when my colleague and I saw a sneak preview of the collaboration between Shopbop’s in-house label, Le Bop, and Julia Berolzheimer, we nearly squealed with delight.

Recent findings suggest that the collection hits all the right notes. It’s colorful. It’s fun yet sophisticated. And for Berolzheimer, the collaboration felt like a full-circle moment. “I have been a customer of Shopbop since the very beginning of my blog (15 years ago!),” Berolzheimer exclusively told ELLE in an email. “Even back then, Shopbop was a destination for style inspiration and discovery...All of that still holds true for the retailer today. When their design team reached out to me last year to co-design a collection for their private label, Le Bop, it was a no-brainer.”.

The collection features taffeta and satiny fabrics adorned with fringe, tonal animal prints, brocade jackets, and jacquard knits. The rich color palette includes dusty rose, chartreuse, espresso, and ocean blue. It is, I must admit, perfect for party dressing that feels a bit unexpected.

According to recent reports, “The inspiration came naturally,” Berolzheimer says. “It stemmed from my personal style and what I love and want to wear around the holidays. I call my style ‘polished maximalist,’ and the collection is just that. There are some bold statement pieces and coordinating sets, which I love to style together, but you can also wear them separately for a more pared-down look. What I love most about this collection is how you can mix and match the pieces for any festive occasion and continue to style them beyond the holiday season.”.

The Le Bop x Julia Berolzheimer collection is available now on Shopbop.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, November 16, Princess Kate and Prince William landed in Mumbai, India, for their first overseas royal tour in four years. The last time the pair made an international state visit was when they traveled to the Caribbean in the spring of 2022 to celebrate the late Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee.

Now, the Prince and Princess of Wales have hit the road again for the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards, which are being hosted in Asia for the first time ever. The annual prize, founded by Prince William with an inaugural ceremony in 2021 and set to last until 2030, celebrates innovators who are breaking ground in the environmentalism space.

Recent findings suggest that while it was declared back in February that William would be traveling for the ceremony, it was confirmed only this past weekend that Kate would be joining him. This marks her first major trip with William since her 2024 cancer diagnosis and eventual remission (she also took a solo trip to Italy this May).

Industry observers note that the 2026 Earthshot ceremony takes place on November 17, but Kate and William are spending a total of three days in India. They began their trip with a visit to Ballard Estate, the business and shopping district of Mumbai. There, the Prince and Princess of Wales played a bit of gully cricket, took a ride on the metro, and visited local vendors and performers. Then, on day two, they stopped by the Bandra Worli Sea Link promenade and attended the Children’s Earthshot ceremony before dressing up for the official event.

For the rest of their time abroad, the royals will be “celebrating innovation, sustainability, youth leadership, and the enduring connections between the United Kingdom and India,” per their office at Kensington Palace.

Ahead, see all the best photos of Kate and William from their overseas tour of Mumbai.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (695 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elle ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Wood, Glass, Porcelain, and Beyond: Jewelry’s Alternative Material Crush

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Industry observers note that one of the greatest things about the best kinds of jewelry is that it has no limits.
  • On the runways recently, we’ve seen Chanel and Dries Van Noten toy with glass necklaces, Margiela play with porcelain (in the form of an ASMR-worthy dress that was an undercover nod to the house’s famous ’90s vest made of the material) as well as multilayered tidbits in standout pieces like Celine’s charm necklaces.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that one of the greatest things about the best kinds of jewelry is that it has no limits. Unlike clothing, it can pretty much be made out of anything, so long as it’s durable. Glass, in jewelry, dates as far back as around 3500 BCE in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, via beads and carvings. Yet all these years later, designers are revisiting the humble material, along with wood, porcelain, and beyond. It makes sense: We’re definitely in an era of experimental jewelry, and materials that push beyond the typical precious metals and gemstones allow for bolder shapes and silhouettes, with major impact. Enter: wooden pendants, glass rings, and porcelain chains.

On the runways recently, we’ve seen Chanel and Dries Van Noten toy with glass necklaces, Margiela play with porcelain (in the form of an ASMR-worthy dress that was an undercover nod to the house’s famous ’90s vest made of the material) as well as multilayered tidbits in standout pieces like Celine’s charm necklaces.

It has been revealed that likewise, fine jewelers are integrating various materials into their work. Marla Aaron, for instance, reimagined her Lock connector pendant in an official collaboration with Nymphenburg porcelain. Marie Lichtenberg makes beautiful dice pendants rendered in black ebony and diamonds. Anna Maccieri Rossi recently released an entire collection dedicated to wood, including chunky necklaces and carved bangles set with gemstones. “I love wood because it is a living material, warm and natural,” she said of the collection. “This material offers me the chance to dream and work on a large scale, with a bolder approach.”.

The cost of gold rapidly ascended in 2025, reaching an all-time nominal record high of $5,589.38 per troy ounce in January 2026. Driven by historic market shifts and a broader surge in precious metal prices, this sharp economic rise has dramatically reshaped how fashion insiders, collectors, and everyday jewelry lovers approach their collections. As traditional solid gold pieces become increasingly rare financial splurges, buyers are actively diversifying their wardrobes with creative, tactile alternatives. In addition to gravitating toward vintage sterling silver and archival heirlooms, jewelry aficionados are now getting their fix with these alternative materials—ranging from hand-carved wood and delicate hand-blown glass to sculptural porcelain and unconventional metals.

Some designers, too, are looking to build and reinvent the legacy of those who came before them. “I think when most people hear ‘glass jewelry,’ a pretty specific image comes to mind,” Colin Keane Lynch of Keane New York tells ELLE. “I’m interested in building on that history while exploring some of the less familiar possibilities.” Lynch, who has devoted his life to working with glass, designs sculptural glass petal rings and sinuous cuffs, all made to order. “Another thing I love about glass is its ability to take on the appearance of so many different materials through explorations of form, texture, and color. It also allows me to create things that might be difficult or even impossible to achieve in other materials.”.

Industry observers note that much like the language and energy of crystals and gemstones, others are interested in these materials because of what they represent. Take Thatch, for instance. Founded by Amy Goin and Laura Laing, the brand sells huge wooden heart pendants as well as fish-shaped wooden bangles and charms. “We feel that wood holds energy the same way gemstones do,” states Goin. “A different kind of energy. Something quieter and more grounded. It’s soulful and raw. We love the bohemian beauty of wood, paired with a touch of gold and sparkle.”.

For today’s designers, the most precious thing about jewelry is the possibility.

#43052. The Best Coffee-Table Books to Gift Your Beautiful, Discerning Friends

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1068 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

The Best Coffee-Table Books to Gift Your Beautiful, Discerning Friends

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that every year holidays come around, and a slight panic sets in at the thought of finding gifts that the people you love will get excited about—and that will make them feel seen.
  • From fashion monographs to punk rock album covers to a guide to medieval wellness, we promise that we’ve found something that will thrill even your most cynical friend.
  • Richard Avedon was undoubtedly one of the greatest photographers of the 20th century and this collection gathers his work for Harper’s Bazaar from 1944 to 1965.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that every year holidays come around, and a slight panic sets in at the thought of finding gifts that the people you love will get excited about—and that will make them feel seen. The real trick is to keep a list throughout the year of everything you see that reminds you of this person or that person. But because sometimes you don’t write things down because you’re “sure you’ll remember,” and because even if you do, we need all the help we can get in discovering cool things, we’ve put together a list of our favorite coffee-table books to give (and to receive, if we’re being honest) this year.

From fashion monographs to punk rock album covers to a guide to medieval wellness, we promise that we’ve found something that will thrill even your most cynical friend.

Richard Avedon was undoubtedly one of the greatest photographers of the 20th century and this collection gathers his work for Harper’s Bazaar from 1944 to 1965. As the world experienced generation-defining shifts, Avedon was zeroed in on his style, creating indelible images that would go on to change fashion. Bonus? It pairs perfectly with Ron Howard’s documentary on the photographer, also titled simply Avedon.

This massive pink tome, assembled by Coppola herself from her own collection of photographs, scripts, collages, and all manner of feminine detritus, offers a revealing and inspirational look at the director’s process and world-building.

It has been revealed that with wit and humor, medievalist Larisa Grollemond sheds light on the way humans lived—and thrived(?)—during the middle ages. Is it true they never bathed? Did they have practice birth control? Were witches in fact, doctors? This books holds the answers.

In a recent development, raymond Pettibon may now be a certified blue-chip artist, but he began his career in the 1970s drawing flyers and record covers for punk bands in Southen California like Minutemen and Black Flag. (He also designed their iconic four-bar logo, which has now been meme-fied.) This book collects his musical body of work, which also includes the Foo Fighters and Lana del Rey—that’s his work on the cover of Norman Fucking Rockwell.

The elusive Martin Margiela may very well be the designer that has most influenced contemporary fashion. Nowhere is that more evident than in this book that looks at the time when the Belgian designer was at the helm of Hermés. The enduring appeal of the collections he created from 1997 to 2002 would go on to set the tone for the whole quiet luxury moment we’ve been living under—except better.

Jeff Goodwin was the makeup artist for David Lynch’s iconic film Blue Velvet. His personal trove of Polaroid photos capture impromptu behind-the-scenes moments and reveal how he refined the makeup looks; they’re accompanied by his own memories of the filming experience.

How many people’s fashion obsessions began as they endlessly dressed and undressed their dolls—be they Barbie, Bratz, or even American Girl dolls? This tome looks at the symbiotic relationship between dolls and real-life grown-up fashion, zeroing in on the works of designers like Comme des Garçons’ Rei Kawakubo and Viktor & Rolf’s Viktor Horsting and Rolf Snoeren, among others.

This is a book designed to inspire. For “Kitchen Piece,” Ono suggests one “hangs a canvas on a wall” and “throws all the leftovers you have” on it, with the caveat that “you may prepare special food for the piece.” After spending time with Ono’s instructions, one realizes there is art to be found literally everywhere.

This is the only book about Carolyn Bessette Kennedy that one may ever need. Sunita Kumar Nair talks to CBK’s friends and, through a carefully curated edit of images, breaks down her style. She also reveals the true essence of the person behind all those infinitely rebloggable images.

Past Continuous is the name of an exhibit at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in Fresh York that brings together the world of Lee Krasner and her husband Jackson Pollock and looks at their career arcs in tandem. It begins with a selection of their paintings before the pair met, and traces their influences, taking a closer look at how their presences wove in and out of each other’s work.

This tome celebrates America’s 250th anniversary through over 200 pages filled with iconic images that have defined the country throughout its history, from images of cowboys wearing their worn-in Levi’s and immigrants landing at Ellis Island to Martin Luther King and Elvis Presley.

Diane Arbus’s unflinching photographs captured humanity in all its beautiful and exacting rawness. Documents tells the history of her short-lived career through essays, criticism, and other ephemera from 1967 through the present day; it’s a comprehensive guide to understanding her work.

Sources indicate that glen Luchford photographed a few of Prada’s most iconic ad campaigns of the 1990s. This book brings them all together along with alternate shots and test shots, and is an essential for both Prada aficionados and lovers of the decade.

In a recent development, created in 1909 by Arthur E. Waite and Pamela Colman Smith in London, the appropriately titled Waite Smith tarot deck is the most popular deck in the world. This book looks at its history, uncovering the details and meaning of each individual card—and it comes with its own set of cards.

In a recent development, this year, the Fashion Museum Antwerp is celebrating its 40th anniversary with an exhibition dedicated to the “Antwerp Six,” the name the fashion media gave to a group of designers—Dries van Noten, Ann Demeulemeeter, Marina Yee, Dirk Bikkembergs, Walter Van Beirendonck, and Dirk Van Seene—that arrived in London in the mid ’80s fresh after their graduation from the Royal Academy of Fine Art. For those who can’t make it to Belgium to see the show, the book may prove to be the next best thing, chock full of photographs, illustrations, newspaper clippings, and essays. They may not have all become household names, but their influence can still be felt on the runways today.

In a recent development, brianna Capozzi’s unique view of womanhood has made her one of the most sought-after photographers in fashion. Her latest monograph features a mix of magazine shots of famous singers and actors with images of impromptu shoots staged with her best friends. The result is a visual shot of adrenaline and a reminder that girls—well, women—just wanna have fun!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like much of the TikTok generation, I spend way too much time looking for style inspo on social media.
  • Hollywood’s cool girls are squeezing every last wear out of fall, wearing silk midi skirts, sheer tops, and cape-like scarves.
  • It has been revealed that while I can’t recreate every ensemble on the internet, I can round up the seven autumn outfits most on my mind, ranked by how eager I am to make them my own before the temps drop for good.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like much of the TikTok generation, I spend way too much time looking for style inspo on social media. While that sometimes means letting the dishes pile up in favor of a few extra minutes of scroll time, I rarely miss a street-style moment. Whether it’s Hailey Bieber in a date-night outfit or Taylor Swift in this season’s hottest color combination, I’ve been stowing away fall outfit inspiration for the final stretch of the season.

Hollywood’s cool girls are squeezing every last wear out of fall, wearing silk midi skirts, sheer tops, and cape-like scarves. Beyond fall essentials like trench coats and dark-wash denim, they’re also reaching for this year’s breakout trends, including maraschino-cherry-colored accessories and striped pullover sweaters, keeping their seasonal rotation fresh before winter takes over.

It has been revealed that while I can’t recreate every ensemble on the internet, I can round up the seven autumn outfits most on my mind, ranked by how eager I am to make them my own before the temps drop for good. Keep reading for late-fall outfit inspo to carry you into the holiday season.

Industry observers note that on the set of Die Alive, Zoë Kravitz made a case for laid-back elegance and an unexpectedly bright fall color choice. The slinky midi skirt is polished, while the basic gray tank is casual. The trench coat makes the outfit perfect for chilly weather, with a pair of chocolate pumps elevating the style. Consider this your go-to look for weekend brunch aims and cocktails with the girls alike.

Selena Gomez put a fresh spin on the capsule wardrobe, creating a monochromatic outfit using closet staples, including sleek capris, mesh pointed-toe heels, and a quilted cinched bag. However, instead of a basic black tee, she reached for a sheer iteration, turning the simple ensemble into a fresh and fun look. To pull it off for a chilly night, I’d add a leather bomber jacket.

Kristen Bell managed to wear just about every style trend at once—without it looking like a slop wardrobe. Her striped pullover served as the base, with coordinated fall-coded colors sprinkled throughout the rest of her outfit. Her dark-wash, wide-leg jeans reminded me why denim is an autumn classic, and I officially want her glove flats. However, it was Bell’s cherry-red beanie and merlot Chanel handbag that injected personality into her look.

It has been revealed that I’m all about a cozy fall wardrobe, but when date night rolls around, I want something a bit more elevated and sleek. Ashley Graham understood the assignment, wearing a silky plunge halterneck top and draped, gray trousers. While she opted for open-toe sandals, pointed, closed-toe pumps can beat the chill.

Karlie Kloss’ chic look is a nod to office wear. Her polished autumnal look features closet basics, including a white button-up shirt, above-the-knee skirt, and ballet flats. Kloss added an extra dose of flair by intentionally draping a black shawl across her shoulders, making it the perfect look for strolling Fifth Avenue and museum hopping alike.

Industry observers note that sometimes the best looks are the simplest. Daisy Edgar-Jones layered a classic white T-shirt underneath a sapphire-blue trench coat, taking a closet basic and elevating it with an unexpected twist. Light-washed, straight-leg jeans elongated her frame, and timeless black pumps turned a casual look into a polished ensemble.

Recent findings suggest that elizabeth Debicki played with fall textures, reaching for a bold leopard-print turtleneck sweater and slick leather pants. Leopard print is both timeless and trendy, which makes it especially easy to style. It’s the ideal outfit for a night on the town, perfectly cozy yet fashion-forward.

#43042. Latest Update: Robert Pattinson’s Hair Is Already 007 Material

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (435 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Robert Pattinson’s Hair Is Already 007 Material

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (435 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whether you like it or not (or placed bets on Kalshi), Robert Pattinson is our next James Bond.
  • Let’s review the canon for a moment.
  • Pattinson’s hair might be naturally light brown, but a darker ‘do is hardly out of the question for the actor’s upcoming transformation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether you like it or not (or placed bets on Kalshi), Robert Pattinson is our next James Bond. During the years-long process in casting 007, we used our best detective skills to narrow down the field to who would join His Majesty’s Secret Service. And if you were going by hair type alone, well, Pattinson makes a rather compelling case.

Let’s review the canon for a moment. In the 1957 novel From Russia, with Love, Bond creator Ian Fleming describes the spy’s mane thusly: “The hair was black, parted on the left, and carelessly brushed so that a thick black comma fell down over the right eyebrow.”.

Pattinson’s hair might be naturally light brown, but a darker ‘do is hardly out of the question for the actor’s upcoming transformation. For his turn as Bruce Wayne in The Batman, he dyed his hair to a darker, almost pitch-black hue. The rest of Fleming’s description fits the actor nicely, particularly the bit about being “carelessly brushed.” In real life, the actor’s hair is rarely anything approaching immaculate. Even at more formal engagements, it tends to retain a certain studied dishevelment, with stray strands escaping an otherwise respectable comb-through. Fleming’s famous “comma,” after all, isn’t a carefully sculpted curl. It’s simply a lock of hair allowed to fall where it pleases, which just so happens to be very on trend in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that we got our first glimpse of the 40-year-old actor taking on the role in a video posted by the official James Bond X account where he’s seen stepping out of the shadows pointing a gun at something (or someone) just outside the frame. It’s hard to tell whether the golden lighting is playing tricks on his hair color, but the accompanying promotional image certainly seems to suggest a shade of black. Plus, his hair’s parted on the correct side.

It has been revealed that it’s worth noting that Daniel Craig’s casting as Bond was initially met with considerable resistance, much of it centered on one detail: He’s blonde. Fleming’s Bond, after all, was famously dark-haired, and Craig represented a departure from the physical template established by the novels and previous screen incarnations. We know how that turned out. Craig went on to deliver one of the most celebrated interpretations of 007, proving that a little deviation from the source material needn’t be a deal-breaker.

Pattinson will still need to prove himself to be agile in a tuxedo, nimble behind the wheel, and thirsty for a martini or two, but one thing’s sure: He's got the hair down pat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that R ivals has returned to our screens, and Rutshire’s residents are hornier than ever. But Rutag fans might have to hang on a little longer to see them enter their relationship era. Frustrating? Not necessarily, as maybe this intense slow-burn is exactly the reason Rivals has managed to create an age-gap relationship we’re actually rooting for.

There is a lot of awareness around age-gap couples in pop culture right now, and audiences seem very done with the classic younger woman, older man dynamic. Movies like A24’s Babygirl and Amazon’s The Idea of You have gone some way toward challenging outdated tropes around age-related power dynamics, but that still doesn’t erase how Hollywood handled things in the past (Pretty Little Liars and Fifty Shades of Grey come to mind).

Rivals is a bit of an anomaly in how it has tackled Rupert and Taggie’s age-gap relationship so far, and the slower pace seems to have played a very necessary part in that. Rutag’s slow-burn underpins the entire foundation of their connection. What’s working for me personally is that Rupert hasn’t been rushing Taggie emotionally or physically to match where he’s at in his current stage of life. In fact, even though he seems besotted with her—she’s sort of become his moral touchstone—he’s doing his best to stay away from her. He seems to find the idea of letting her down (or fully letting her in) absolutely terrifying, despite how much he clearly cares.

Rivals gains further grace from viewers for its willingness to openly acknowledge Rupert and Taggie’s age gap as being an obstacle to overcome in their relationship, rather than just glossing over it or choosing to pretend it doesn’t exist. Rupert even acknowledges the age gap as being an problem himself by making a promise to Declan in season 1 that he’ll stay away from Taggie. By showing us these hurdles early on, it gives deeper insight into what a relationship would eventually mean for these two and what they’d be up against.

In a recent development, watching Taggie gain life experience and have her own adventures of self-discovery—not everything has to involve Rupert—has helped them remain exciting to us as a potential couple. Her catering business seems to be thriving, for example. The slow-burn gives Taggie the opportunity to forge her own identity and ambitions, which would be vital to have going into a relationship with Rupert, given their differences in life experience. Taggie is slowly blossoming into herself, without falling into that cliché trap of trying to change who she is to impress a man, and that’s empowering and necessary.

As long as Rivals continues to explore the age gap with care and consideration, I think fans will keep rooting for Rutag’s romance, no matter how long the slow-burn takes.

#43028. Why Everything New Looks a Little Vintage Right Now

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (977 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

Why Everything New Looks a Little Vintage Right Now

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, backstage at the Spring 2027 Chanel show in Paris, after a parade of elegantly skirt-suited women strolled beneath an extravagant set of birds suspended midflight, Matthieu Blazy told a story of picking his teenage nephew up from school.
  • One look in particular felt more akin to how someone would dress to attend the Chanel show rather than to walk it—an old-school Chanel jacket worn with upcoming Chanel shoes, a pair of black trousers, eclectic jewelry and an old belt.
  • It has been revealed that loving and collecting vintage (or better yet, holding onto pieces until they became vintage) was once the domain of fashion insiders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, backstage at the Spring 2027 Chanel show in Paris, after a parade of elegantly skirt-suited women strolled beneath an extravagant set of birds suspended midflight, Matthieu Blazy told a story of picking his teenage nephew up from school. Observing the students, he was struck by the irreverent way they dressed. “They wear a lot of vintage. They are not dictated by a decade—they are a lot more free,” he told Bazaar. “They wear something from the ’30s, ’50s, ’70s. I wanted to expand on that.”.

One look in particular felt more akin to how someone would dress to attend the Chanel show rather than to walk it—an old-school Chanel jacket worn with upcoming Chanel shoes, a pair of black trousers, eclectic jewelry and an old belt. It wasn’t an anomalous look; the vintagey vibes loomed large. Knee-length skirt suits were styled with heaps of necklaces. Men’s shirting was mixed with relaxed tailoring and leather separates; tiny white tank tops peeked from beneath tweed jackets festooned with oversized, floral brooches.

It has been revealed that loving and collecting vintage (or better yet, holding onto pieces until they became vintage) was once the domain of fashion insiders. But today, young people are growing up native to the secondhand market. (According to ThredUp’s 2026 Resale Report, 62 percent of Gen Z shopped secondhand last year.) As they age, dressing from a closet that contains clothing from multiple style eras has become inevitable. And designers are taking notice.

It has been revealed that just as the Dolce & Gabbana show was about to start in Milan a week before the Chanel show, the loudspeaker turned on to regale the audience on “the wardrobes of Sicily’s grand houses. Clothes once worn by great-grandmothers, grandmothers, mothers, aunts and daughters. A slip dress is worn over a jacket, antique lace meets contemporary pieces, lingerie and eveningwear coexist, and the precious and the everyday merge in an unexpected balance.” The styling made it feel as if a young woman pilfered grandma’s closet, mixing an antique, pussy bow blouse with embellished and ripped jeans or pairing a D&G baby tee with a leopard-trimmed, tweedy jacket.

Sources indicate that at Gucci, Demna dissected the archetypes of the bourgeoisie, including “the rebellious aristocrat.” A series of looks paired variations of rugby shirts, pleated tartan skirts, puff-shaped bomber jackets with oversized belts adorned with horsebits and heaps of jewelry piled onto necklines. It’s what a “blue-blooded child of an aristocrat might wear to the private school that she hates,” Demna mused after the show. Within that layered ensemble, he defined a character: Her kilt is part of her school uniform; her rugby polo and leather jacket were mined from a thrift store or her dad’s closet. She wore all these pieces together with no regard for where or what era they came from.

Recent findings suggest that the idea of dressing “vintage” on a runway is inherently contradictory. The runways are a place of newly introduced; vintage is, by definition, old. But the concept is more about adding depth and texture to an ensemble than it is about the age of the garment itself. It’s not about, as in seasons past, garments that are distressed to look worn and weathered. It’s about achieving a kind of idiosyncrasy in a landscape that had become samey and polished and “quiet luxury.” It’s about a desire for irreverence.

The Row is a spectacular case study here, particularly as it was one of the brands that ushered in the minimalist look of the early 2020s. So how to evolve without alienating your customer? For Spring 2027, the Olsen twins draped and knotted antique linens, lace, and doilies over their typical rotation of sleek, black trousers and perfectly mussed trench coats. Models wore layers of dainty beads or single chunky necklaces that nodded subtly towards eclecticism or bohemian.

It has been revealed that fashion must contend and engage with vintage; increasingly, it is just a part of how people shop. As the secondhand market gains traction, it presents new challenges; houses are in constant competition with their own archives. Just look at the resurgences of secondhand Pucci and Etro from the early 2000s. Many have embraced reissues: Chloé’s Maxime wedge or the McQueen skull scarf, for example, shown tucked into contemporary collections of recent years. Of course, creative directors at legacy houses have always had to find ways to be in conversation with their archives and predecessors. The greatest designers, however, manage to use this formula to their advantage.

Take Blazy at Chanel, for instance. He must contend with Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel’s founding legacy of the early and mid-1900s in addition to Karl Lagerfeld’s from the ’80s through the 2010s. The idea of a knee-length skirt suit in nubby fabric could seem retro, but Blazy leaned into it instead of pushing against it. He didn’t rewrite the idea entirely, but shifted our perception with subtle tweaks in materials, textures, and styling. He even sent Gabrielle’s original 2.55 bag down the runway, paired with a gauzy white cocktail dress and then again later with a black skirt suit.

According to recent reports, ralph Lauren mined his own greatest hits for a spring collection that was a glorious mishmash of old and fresh, clashing Americana Westernwear and prep with tropes of the English aristocracy, and even utilitarian workwear. He strung models’ waistcoats with pocket watches, paired brocade evening jackets with distressed denim, and matched ruffled-collar blouses with metallic skirts.

It’s that dialogue between items that conjures the feel of someone who wears vintage, someone who curates their closet with stylistic depth, nuance, and contrast. What young people achieve with aplomb is decidedly difficult to manufacture. But that’s what makes it so desirable. It turns runway models from mannequins into characters and makes you want to learn their stories.

We’re so back. Taylor Swift just arrived on the 2026 CMAs red carpet in anticipation of her first time performing at the annual award show in 13 (naturally!) years. Tay indicated up wearing a neon yellow strapless gown with a gathered front:.

Industry observers note that the singer is nominated for “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5, and rumor has it she’ll be performing the song tonight (though it’s also possible she could surprise everyone with “Patient Zero” or something else off The Life of a Showgirl). #43013. It’s Time to Talk About “Duty Sex”

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

It’s Time to Talk About “Duty Sex”

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are certain things that belong on your chore list: Doing laundry, washing dishes, taking the trash out, scrubbing the toilet.
  • Industry observers note that duty sex typically stems from good intentions, Marisa Derr, LMFT explains.
  • This isn’t just an unnecessary pressure that can be demoralizing, it’s also just super unsexy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are certain things that belong on your chore list: Doing laundry, washing dishes, taking the trash out, scrubbing the toilet. Sex, as you can see, is not one of those things—and it shouldn’t be. And yet, “duty sex” has become a pretty recognizable term in today’s relationships.

Industry observers note that duty sex typically stems from good intentions, Marisa Derr, LMFT explains. This happens when one partner wants to keep the peace or protect the relationship. It’s when you have sex because for some reason or another, you feel like you have to—not because you’re worried for your safety, but you believe that the success of your relationship lies on “fulfilling” some sexual duty.

This isn’t just an unnecessary pressure that can be demoralizing, it’s also just super unsexy.

“The problem is that sex out of obligation teaches the body that intimacy is another task, and desire fades even more,” she notes. “Over time, the partner initiating feels rejected, and the partner saying yes feels used, even though neither one wants that.”.

In a recent development, there’s an important distinction between duty sex and what we call “willing consent.” Willing consent is when you’re not necessarily feeling desire for your partner in the moment, but you consent to a sexual interaction with them because you’re open to desire showing up. It’s like when you’re not feeling particularly hungry, but you know that you really enjoy a certain meal so you go out to eat at the spot anyway. Duty sex is born from obligation, rather than curiosity—like eating that weird casserole your aunt brings on Thanksgiving when you really don’t want to, but do anyway because you prefer to not ruffle any feathers.

When did sex with our partners become that weird casserole or equivalent to scrubbing the toilet?

According to a recent study in Evolutionary Psychology, duty sex can be rooted in fear: Fear that a partner will cheat, fear that one could be less attractive than their partners and need to somehow “make up for it,” and fear that a partner will lose interest in them.

And while we typically assign duty sex as something that women mostly do—particularly because of the pressures to perform that disproportionately affect women—the study showed that men were having duty sex at similar rates as women. Though, more research is needed to find out if there is a difference between why men have duty sex and why women do it.

The thing that most people having duty sex had in common was that they were in long-term relationships.

According to recent reports, “Couples can start worrying about how often they're having sex, rather than whether they're actually enjoying it,” sex educator Anna Richards tells Cosmopolitan. “But intimacy shouldn't be about meeting a target or keeping score. It should be something you both genuinely want.”.

It has been revealed that sex should be about feeling pleasure and connecting with your partner in a fun, sexy, and intimate way. But for some couples, somewhere in the midst of all of the responsibilities of everyday life, sexual desire was put on the back burner. And instead of working to get it back, people are essentially forcing themselves to have duty sex to maintain their relationships. We need a serious overhaul of partnered sex!

In a recent development, “You can't demand desire, but you can create an environment where it has room to grow,” Richard indicates. Think about what the study said about why people have duty sex: they’re afraid of losing their partner. And one of the ways to bridge this gap of insecurity is to foster a relationship that comes with reassurance. If you’re the one finding yourself having duty sex, communicate with your partner about the pressure you feel. Talking about your needs—whether they come in the form of emotional security, verbal affirmations, or quality time—can help your partner learn how to help you foster desire. And if you’re the partner that’s noticing your S.O. initiate sex just to check it off a list, maybe it’s time to think about whether you’re reassuring them enough in the relationship. Do you create an environment of trust and comfort? Are you caring? Do you help them with their daily tasks?

One of the best ways to remove sex off your to-do list and onto your want-to-do list is to take it off your list completely. That may sound counterintuitive, but Richards says it helps alleviate the pressure.

According to recent reports, “Intimacy doesn't always have to lead to the bedroom,” she says. Flirting, spending quality time together, being affectionate, making each other feel appreciated, talking about what you enjoy—these can all help rebuild a connection between you and your partner.

“Sometimes removing the expectation is exactly what allows desire to return naturally,” she indicates. You also need to make sure that your relationship is a place where saying “no” feels safe.

“A yes only means something when a no is fully okay,” Derr explains. “Pressure, sulking, or keeping score kills desire.”.

Sources indicate that it’s also about the little things. Saying “thank you” when they do something nice, touching each other throughout the day, complimenting each other, and just being a good partner can all lend themselves into reigniting desire.

Recent findings suggest that life is way too short to be having sex because you feel like you have to. Plus, any healthy and happy relationship would not foster an environment where sex feels like a duty in the first place. Yes, making a relationship work longterm does take work and effort—but that doesn’t mean that every aspect of your relationship should feel like work. The parts that are meant to be fueled by fun and curiosity (like sex) should remain fun. And the second sex starts feeling like a chore, it may be time to clear your checklist and make reconnecting your first priority.
